summary: Marion County, OR ODF lookout: 1938 tower destroyed by the 1962 Columbus Day Hurricane, 1965 portable-cab replacement; sources disagree on whether any tower stands today.

facts.design: 82-foot timber tower with L-6 cab (1938, per Forest Lookouts); firelookout.com instead gives a 34-foot steel tower with 7x7 cab
facts.status_note: FFLA list shows standing; Forest Lookouts has a bare Removed note under its 1965 entry; firelookout.com says the superstructure is still there

corrections.why: Sources conflict. The FFLA list shows standing, Forest Lookouts has an unexplained Removed note under its 1965 entry, and firelookout.com says the superstructure is still there.

corrections.proposed: 82-foot timber tower with L-6 cab (1938, destroyed 1962); the standing structure, if any, is the 1965 replacement
corrections.why: The L-6 cab and 25 m height describe the 1938 tower that Forest Lookouts says was destroyed in 1962. The 1965 replacement is a different structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1938 tower is an 82-foot timber tower with L-6 cab per Forest Lookouts, and a 34-foot steel tower with 7x7 cab per firelookout.com. Not resolved. The record keeps the Forest Lookouts design, which also matches the 25 m height.
A 1939 district report gives 100 feet, against the 82 feet of the 1938 entry. The record's 25.0 m (82 ft) is kept.

The FFLA list shows the tower standing, Forest Lookouts has a bare Removed note under its 1965 entry that does not say what it covers, and firelookout.com says the superstructure is still there. Not resolved; the story says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Three sources disagree on the 1938 tower's material, height and whether any tower stands now. The Removed tag on the Forest Lookouts page sits under the 1965 entry and may refer to the portable cab rather than the whole site. No access or current-condition source was found, and no ODF page was read. The 1938 Forest Log item was used only for the lookout's name; its medical detail was left out. The firelookout.com entry itself is short (R.I.P. 1938-?, 34 ft steel, 1965 crank-up replacement).
